title: U.S. House · New York's 11th Congressional District
area: Staten Island and part of southern Brooklyn (Bay Ridge and neighboring areas).

context.text: Michael DeCillis defeated Allison Ziogas in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 61.4% to 37.1% (10,455 to 6,309 votes).

Allison Ziogas, who lost the Democratic primary but had also qualified for the general-election ballot on the "Affordable & Safe" party line, suspended her congressional campaign in 2026 for health reasons; Ballotpedia now lists her as withdrawn from the general election.
Nicole Malliotakis is seeking re-election after advancing unopposed through the Republican and Conservative Party primaries, which were both canceled.

candidates.name: Nicole Malliotakis
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed through the Republican and Conservative Party primaries

priorities.text: Supported the 2025 budget reconciliation law ("Big Beautiful Bill"), citing provisions making the 2017 tax cuts permanent, quadrupling the SALT deduction cap to $40,000, and exempting most seniors' Social Security income from federal tax.
priorities.quote: Today is a historic day for Staten Islanders, Brooklynites, and families across the nation who have been calling for meaningful tax relief.

priorities.text: Has pushed to end New York City's congestion pricing tolling program and discussed the issue directly with President Trump.

As a member of the Ways and Means Committee, has focused legislative work on tax administration and IRS accountability issues, including bills addressing stolen tax refund checks and fraudulent return preparers.

positions.summary: In a 2025 statement backed the Justice Department lawsuit against New York City's sanctuary policies and called for the city to cooperate with ICE detainer requests; in June 2026 highlighted $38 billion for ICE in the Secure America Act.
positions.quote: Restoring public safety in our communities starts with New York City cooperating with ICE’s detainer requests.

record.text: Introduced H.R. 9499, the Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act, which passed the House unanimously on September 16, 2026; the bill limits the indefinite statute of limitations on fraudulent tax returns to cases where the taxpayer knowingly intended to commit fraud, rather than cases where a dishonest preparer acted alone.

Co-introduced with Rep. James McGovern (D-MA) H.R. 5439, the Medically Tailored Home-Delivered Meals Program Pilot Act, which passed the House Ways and Means Committee; it creates a 6-year Medicare pilot program at 40 hospitals delivering medically tailored meals to Medicare beneficiaries with diet-affected chronic diseases after hospital discharge.

Introduced H.R. 9771, the Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act of 2026, which passed the House Ways and Means Committee; it bars large tax-exempt organizations from making contributions to political committees for two years after receiving a gift from a foreign national and imposes escalating penalties, including suspension of tax-exempt status after a third violation.
Announced $1,000,000 in federal funding for CCTV security upgrades at NYCHA's Berry Houses development in Staten Island.

priorities.text: Says Congress needs stronger checks on executive power, comparing the need to post-Watergate congressional reforms, so that policy is not set by executive action alone.
Wants to reduce the tax burden on working people and require higher earners to "pay their fair share" to address rising costs for groceries, gas, healthcare, and housing.
As a former teacher, says he will oppose efforts to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education and push for more investment in public education.
Does not accept money from corporate PACs or PACs that lobby on behalf of a single foreign nation.

positions.summary: Supports moving to a single-payer healthcare system that eliminates co-pays and deductibles, and opposes Republican-enacted cuts to ACA subsidies, Medicaid and Medicare.

Says immigration enforcement is necessary for people who have committed crimes but that ICE is operating unconstitutionally and should be abolished as currently structured, citing warrantless searches and arrests.
Supports universal background checks, gun licensing, and an assault weapons ban; holds the 2026 Moms Demand Action candidate distinction.
Supports codifying Roe v. Wade and says decisions about reproductive care belong to women, not government.
Wants to reduce the tax burden on working-class families while requiring billionaires and large corporations to pay a higher share.
Supports federal climate action, including penalties for water and air pollution and infrastructure investment to protect shorelines from storms and flooding.

researchNotes: Allison Ziogas won a ballot line via primary but suspended her campaign for health reasons before the general election and is not included as a candidate, per Ballotpedia's current withdrawn-candidate listing. Per the research brief, Rep. Malliotakis's federal floor votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script; her record here focuses on sponsored legislation and committee actions not covered by that process. Michael DeCillis's campaign biography and Ballotpedia both describe his New York State Assembly role as Chief of Staff and Director of Legislation for an Assembly member, not as an elected Assembly member himself; a check of the current nyassembly.gov member roster found no member by that name, so no Assembly voting record exists for him and none is included here.
